title: Eight-variable Extra Trees model separates nontuberculous mycobacteria from tuberculosis
summary: An Extra Trees model using eight routine laboratory variables was developed in Hospital A (n = 1,090; 130 NTM) and evaluated frozen in Hospital B (n = 1,160; 128 NTM). External AUC was 0.849 and AUPRC 0.505; at the fixed threshold sensitivity was 67.2% and specificity 83.7%, with 42 of 128 external NTM cases below threshold. The study is retrospective and the model cannot support stand-alone diagnosis.
ai_technology: Extra Trees machine-learning classifier on eight routine laboratory variables
organization: North China University of Science and Technology

evidence.tested: The frozen model was evaluated on an independent hospital, with a post-hoc nested analysis (AUC 0.875).
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance, reference-diagnosis timing and clinical impact are not tested. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: An Extra Trees model estimated the probability of NTM versus tuberculosis from routine lab results.
